newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ASM Litho H1 net seen flat, up slightly.
newsitem.headline: ASM Litho H1 net seen flat, up slightly.

text.p: First half results from Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASM Lithography NV next Wednesday are likely to be flat or only slightly higher, held back mainly by past slackness in chip markets, analysts said on Thursday.
Analysts' forecasts for first half net profit range from as low as 95 million guilders to above 110 million, compared with 100.7 million in the first half of 1996.

Sales at the firm are seen higher, reflecting increased demand for its new generation Deep Ultraviolet (DUV) machines, and fundamental market conditions are seen improving during the second half and in the coming few years.

"The first half is really a problem and ASML is in the lucky position that its products are in high demand, it sort of escapes the (overall) industry slowdown," said analyst Bert Siebrand of SNS Securities.

"In terms of chip markets for this year it's still looking fairly weak in terms of year on year volumes. But when you go to equipment for next year I think we're going to look for 20 to 30 percent higher equipment sales," he said.
Analysts said relatively slack demand for chips seemed to have bottomed out late last year, while trends in semiconductor equipment makers lagged that cycle by around six months.

"The chip sector bottomed in October last year and the semiconductor equipment sector bottomed in April this year," said Siebrand, adding "The fourth quarter and next year look a lot better (for ASML)".

Pieter van Gelder of Delta Lloyd Bank sees first half 1997 net profit rising to 104.6 million guilders on sales up to 641 million guilders from 597 million, partly reflecting the increased volumes in DUV machines.
"They've already mentioned that revenue would be slightly higher but that net income would be in the same area as last year," said Van Gelder.

At the full year 1996 stage ASML chief executive Willem Maris said the company expected a "moderate" first half 1997 performance, anticipating demand for semi-conductor equipment could strengthen in the second half.

Eric de Graaf of ING Barings expects first half 1997 net profit to dip fractionally, hurt by higher research and development costs, although that should be offset to some extent by currency impacts from the weak guilder.
"The positive effects of their DUV sales won't really take off until the second half of the year, (and) there will be higher costs for research and development," he said.
Philips Electronics NV holds a minority stake in ASML. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
